input.quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
input.rationale: § 3.2 provides automatic renewal but requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice of non-renewal, exceeding the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window (and well short of our preferred 30-day opt-out with a 60-day vendor reminder). The operative fix states the window as "60 days" in the clause itself. The renewal clause permits no uplift — renewal is for a term equal in duration to the previous term on the existing terms — so the price-increase element is not engaged; IBM's separate unilateral price-change right in § 13.1 (available only after 12 months, on 90 days' notice, with a fee-free Customer exit) is a change-of-terms mechanic and is not double-flagged here. Renewal-term length mirroring the previous term is a preferred-level point noted rather than redlined; if any Service Option Attachment carries a term longer than 12 months, we would escalate to fix the renewal term at 12 months to avoid automatic multi-year renewals.

ops.oldText: at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term
ops.newText: at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from ninety (90) days to 60 days so an early deadline cannot lock us into a further automatic renewal term; 60 days is our fallback position (our preferred is a 30-day opt-out with a 60-day renewal reminder).
proposal.summary: Shorten the § 3.2 non-renewal notice window from 90 days to 60 days.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
